mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) within 6 months of signal activation, or 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where GDP y/y growth accelerates by > 2pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate over the previous 3 months, indicating a rapidly tightening labor market, will lead to wage inflation and reduced profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE drops > 0.5pp in 3 months, or wage inflation fails to materialize (Atlanta Fed Wage Growth Tracker < 3% y/y).

mechanism_narrative: When the ISM Manufacturing Index (proxied by INDPRO) falls below 45, indicating a manufacturing recession, S&P 500 returns will be negative over the next 60 trading days as industrial companies' earnings decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where INDPRO < 45, or manufacturing recession fails to materialize (ISM Manufacturing Index remains above 45 for 6 consecutive months).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4%, indicating a restrictive monetary policy, S&P 500 returns will be negative over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs weigh on corporate profits.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4%, or real GDP growth remains above 2% y/y for 6 months after signal activation.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (proxied by HOUST) decline by more than 10% year-over-year, signaling a weakening housing market, consumer spending will slow and S&P 500 returns will be negative over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where HOUST declines > 10% y/y, or housing market activity rebounds (HOUST rises > 5% y/y) within 6 months of signal activation.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) are both rising simultaneously, indicating a potential wage-price spiral, S&P 500 returns will be negative over the next 20 trading days as the Fed tightens policy to combat inflation.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where both UNRATE and FEDFUNDS are rising, or the wage-price spiral fails to materialize (CPI inflation < 3% y/y) within 6 months of signal activation.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is rising by more than 0.5% month-over-month, indicating high inflation and tight monetary policy, S&P 500 returns will be negative over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL m/m > 0.5%, or monetary policy eases (FEDFUNDS declines by > 0.5pp) within 6 months of signal activation.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) is growing by more than 3% year-over-year and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, indicating a strong economy with tight labor markets, S&P 500 returns will be positive over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where GDPC1 y/y > 3% and UNRATE < 4%, or economic growth slows sharply (GDPC1 y/y < 1%) within 6 months of signal activation.
